rv.q: That’s what makes this Seagull a particularly harrowing true story.

But the staging is witty and inventive enough to allow us to understand why the young artist, when still in his twenties, had been invited to direct “The Seagull” at the Theater, the venerable venue where Konstantin Stanislavski first helmed Chekhov’s masterpiece.
Seagull: True Story may have imperfections, but its urgent message forces audiences to confront hard truths about the contentious relationship between politics and theatre.
Indeed, if it wasn’t for Posey’s luminous turn, this “Seagull” would truly deserve “the bird.”
